instructions: Put the rice, 2 cups of water and 1/2 tsp of the salt in a pot over high heat. Bring it to a boil, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 20 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on.
Meanwhile, dice half the onion, dice 1 celery rib and the ham, and mince the garlic. Drain the black-eyed peas in a colander and rinse them under cold water.

Heat the oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the onion, celery and the ham. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion is soft and the ham has a few browned edges.
Add the garlic and stir for 1 minute, until it smells fragrant.
Add the broth and the tomatoes with their juice. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot, then bring it to a boil.
Stir in the peas, turn the heat to medium-low and cover. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. The ham is salty, so go easy.
Serve the peas over the rice.
method_notes: Lead is Southern Bite (5.0 from 9, a fallback with fewer than 20 ratings): onion and celery softened in oil, then broth, smoked ham and tomatoes with green chiles, and black-eyed peas simmered, served over converted rice. Other versions agree on the pork and peas and differ on cut (bacon, kielbasa, ham hock) and cook time. The source uses a bag of frozen peas simmered 30 to 35 minutes; canned peas, drained and rinsed, only need 15, which keeps the dinner within 45 minutes. Ham, not a hock, so it works on a weeknight. Check the ham and broth labels for gluten.
